## 1) Chart type
A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.
- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Count / magnitude (0, 10.0M, 20.0M, etc.) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height |
| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.
- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Count / magnitude (0, 10.0M, 20.0M, etc.) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height |
| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.
- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Count / magnitude (0, 10.0M, 20.0M, etc.) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height |
| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

raw_comment:
What I noticed - 

I noticed that if there was only 7 days of interventions there were a ton of people who were infected and there were more deaths and hospitalizations than the other intervention periods. I also noticed that after 42 days of intervention there were very little infected and there were only a few hospitalized and deceased. Over the longer stretches of intervention you can clearly see that the curve was being flattened and there were also less deceased when you get above 21 days of intervention. This shows that the social distancing and being careful does end up helping. This means that it is important we keep with it to get this pandemic under control.

## 1) Chart type
A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.
- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Count / magnitude (0, 10.0M, 20.0M, etc.) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height |
| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

I notice that as the number of interventions in previous every-day activities rises in a seemingly marginal way, the amount of cases of the virus goes down in an extremely drastic way. This shows just how beneficial and important social distancing is and how it can save a lot of lives. 

I wonder if these graphs take into account the people who are ignoring the warnings and still interacting with other people. It seems a little unrealistic that everyone fill follows directions even if it is pretty obvious how much good it can do to just change up your daily routine a little bit and avoid contact with other people as much as possible. 

Because this graph does a really good job of showing how important these interventions of daily routine can be I think a good title for the graph might be "How Staying Inside Can Save Millions"

raw_comment: I notice that as an increase in the time that the intervention occurs, so does an increase in the amount of peaks that the infected population has. It appears that with only 7 days of interventions, there is one very distinguishable peak in June with the start of a secondary peak in April. This secondary peak continues to develop while the interventions increase and eventually, a third peak appears to start to develop which may happen in November. This increase in peaks causes the initial distinguishable peak to stretch and approach a further date in time. the distinguishable peak also tends to lose its distinguishability as it flattens, or decreases in amplitude. This shows that the overall infected population, while mostly remaining constant as a sum over time, will decrease in magnitude for each value of time. I wonder what the graphs would look like if the infectious and recovery periods were to decrease. I also wonder what would appear to happen if, rather than the period of intervention all be continuous, if it were to be split up into sections with an equal total amount of days of intervention. This would probably be irrational and ineffective however it still is interesting if it were to happen. A catchy headline for this graph could be “Coronavirus Timeline Contraction Through Intervention”

I notice that as more times passes under school/business closings and social distancing restrictions, the more the COVID-19 infection rates drop. This leads me to claim that with more time under limited social interaction leads to a decrease in infection and death rates due to COVID-19.

This graph is detailing the simulation of estimated death, hospitalization, and infection rates over different increasing periods of intervention days. A good headline for this graph would be "The Effects of Intervention Against a Virus."

## 1) Chart type
A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.
- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Count / magnitude (0, 10.0M, 20.0M, etc.) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height |
| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.

- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

|---|---|---|

| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |

- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

|---|---|---|

| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

## 1) Chart type
A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.
- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Count / magnitude (0, 10.0M, 20.0M, etc.) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height |
| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

## 1) Chart type
A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.
- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Count / magnitude (0, 10.0M, 20.0M, etc.) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height |
| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.
- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Count / magnitude (0, 10.0M, 20.0M, etc.) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height |
| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

raw_comment:
Thanks to all students who responded.  We had so many great catchy headlines that capture the main ideas of the graphs:  "Take Precautions and Avoid the Consequences" by Abby of St. Vincent-St. Mary High School in Akron, Ohio, “Less Intervention. More Infections” by Lily of Seoul, Korea, "The Longer You Stay, the More People You Save" by Rodney of Austin, Texas, and “Stay Inside and Things Will Subside!” by Victoria of Gladeville Middle School in Mt. Juliet, Tennessee.

You can continue to post responses.  Please check back tomorrow --  Thursday afternoon, April 16 to see the Reveal with a link to the original New York Times article, three interactive graphs, some questions about these graphs, and a few Stat Nuggets.

The next graph will be released in two days -- Friday, April 17, with moderation on Wednesday, April 22.  You may respond before, during, or after the live moderation by going to “What's Going On In This Graph?”  The topic --  how our spending habits have changed with Covid-19.

You can see all of the released graphs on the “What’s Going On In This Graph?” homepage.  Or, go to our post “Looking for Graphs to Use in the Classroom? Here Are 34.” for an index by context and an index by type of graph.

The link for the Stat Nuggets archives ishttps://tinyurl.com/StatNuggets.

Signing off – Sharon Hessney of Boston, who goes out only for long walks with a homemade face mask, and Greg Yarnall of Morristown, NJ, who is keeping his quarantine beard for the duration!

image_description:
## 1) Chart type
A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.
- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Count / magnitude (0, 10.0M, 20.0M, etc.) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height |
| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

The more we follow these protocols, the faster the coronavirus will stop spreading.

Therefore, this could have been a result of more spreading because these people would not be as careful since they thought they did not have it. Also, many people cannot afford the tests or get their hands on one, so it is difficult to know the exact number of people infected.

- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |

| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.
- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Count / magnitude (0, 10.0M, 20.0M, etc.) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height |
| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

image_description:
## 1) Chart type
A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.
- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Count / magnitude (0, 10.0M, 20.0M, etc.) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height |
| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

raw_comment:
I noticed how little we are to be forcibly staying inside/being cautious/following social distancing. 

I know that the main issue is the overwhelming number of infected rather than the intensity of the virus itself. I also know that things weren't necessarily anticipated to this degree and despite what our country is doing to fix it, there is bound to be mistakes.  People have lost time they will never get back, and beyond that, loved ones that will never return. I have the same question everybody else does; I ponder the idea that maybe the results of Covid19 would regretfully be dissimilar to a late reaction to influenza. My title might say "Does 49 days really account for human error?"

A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques

- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |

| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

raw_comment:
I noticed that the graphs show the changes in the number of people infected, hospitalized and killed by the virus. Each graph increases from top left to top right in the number of days of interventions each time by 7 days. The x-axis represents the months (January, April, July and October, increasing by 3 months); the y-axis represents the number of people (10 million, 20 million and 30 million, increasing by 10 million). The shaded gray area represents the number of days of intervention. The light red shade is the people infected; the medium red shade is the people hospitalized; the dark red shade is the number of people deceased. 

The light red shaded portion reaches 40 million people and declines dramatically between mid-June and August in the graph that shows only 7 days of intervention at the end of March. The light red shaded portion reaches far less than 10 million people in the graph with 42 days of interventions. Additionally, I noticed that unlike the graph with 7 days of interventions, this graph suggests that there will be a resurgent of cases. 

The viewer can infer that as the number of days of interventions increase, the number of cases and deaths will decrease. Conversely, as the number of days of interventions decreases, the number of cases and deaths will increase. 

I wonder if after 42 days of interventions, the likelihood that infections of Covid-19 would disappear completely.

Headline: Less Intervention; More Infections

A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.
- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Count / magnitude (0, 10.0M, 20.0M, etc.) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height |
| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.
- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Count / magnitude (0, 10.0M, 20.0M, etc.) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height |
| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.
- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Count / magnitude (0, 10.0M, 20.0M, etc.) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height |
| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.

image_description:
## 1) Chart type
A **faceted stacked area chart** (small multiples), with six panels showing time series under different intervention durations.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 6 panels arranged in a 2×3 grid.
- **Stacking**: Three colored area series are stacked within each panel.
- **Annotation band**: Each panel includes a vertical shaded band marking the intervention period, with a “Today” label.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Date / time (Jan., April, July, Oct.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Count / magnitude (0, 10.0M, 20.0M, etc.) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height |
| Health outcome category: Infected / Hospitalized / Deceased | Categorical / nominal | Color/hue; stacked area layers |
| Intervention duration (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 days of interventions) | Ordinal / categorical | Faceting into separate panels; panel titles |
| Intervention period | Temporal interval | Vertical shaded band |
| “Today” marker | Temporal reference | Text label near x-position within shaded band |

Notes: The legend confirms the three outcome categories: **Infected**, **Hospitalized**, and **Deceased**.
